dashboard.gainTotal.explain: Your total gain is the sum of four terms — unrealised gain, realised gain, dividends received, and the fees your broker takes out of your transfers. That sum is its definition: the app adds the four up rather than computing a total separately and trusting that they agree. The fourth term belongs to no security, which is why a table of positions can never show it.
dashboard.ytd.pending: history not rebuilt that far back yet
dashboard.ytd.noPreviousYear: nothing recorded before 1 January, so there is no year to count from yet
dashboard.netContributed.explain: Net contributed: your deposits less your withdrawals, fees excluded. It is the silent denominator of both returns, and the reason the total gain has a fourth term — a fee taken from a transfer leaves your cash without lowering what this figure records.
dashboard.xirr.explain: Money-weighted return: what your deposits actually earned. It is the single annual rate that reconciles everything that entered and left, each on its own date, with what the portfolio is worth today — so money paid in before a rise weighs more than money paid in after it. Returns are computed from the dates of your events.
dashboard.twr.explain: Time-weighted return: how the positions themselves performed, independent of your deposits. Paying money in, or taking it out, moves it by nothing at all, which is what makes two portfolios of different sizes comparable. It depends on the period it covers, and a ranking can reverse inside it. Returns are computed from the dates of your events.
dashboard.awaitingCurrency: Your total value, your net contributions and both returns are waiting for a base currency — nobody has answered that question yet.
dashboard.withoutLedger: A ledger of dated events would add your total value, your net contributions and both returns.
dashboard.empty.title: No events yet
dashboard.empty.body: Everything here is computed from a ledger of dated events. Nothing has been imported or entered yet.
dashboard.chart.area.gain: The gap between the two curves is your total gain.
dashboard.chart.area.unrealised: The gap between the two curves is your unrealised P&L. Your portfolio records no cash movement, so the app cannot tell what you put in from what your positions cost.

currency.untilAnswered: It is fixed the moment you answer it: every amount is recorded in it from then on, and a second answer would reinterpret them rather than convert them. The answer can be given late — it just cannot be taken back.
currency.fixed: Fixed: your amounts are recorded in it, and it cannot be taken back.

firstRun.what.quotes: The app fetches the quotes by itself and computes the rest from your events.
firstRun.what.currency: Everything is reported in a single currency, and that one is yours to choose now.
firstRun.ephemeral: This container keeps nothing: the store sits in its own writable layer and disappears the next time it is recreated. That is a fine way to try the app out — mount a volume to keep it.

shares.gainTotal.explain: The gain of every line of this table, closed positions included — their realised gain and their dividends stay in this figure long after the position itself is gone, and leaving them out would show you a second figure, just as correct, that is not your gain. It is the sum of the three columns below, which is what makes it checkable by eye. One term cannot appear here: the fees your broker takes out of a transfer belong to no security.
shares.value.explain: What you hold, converted into your base currency. A position whose price has never been observed is counted at what it cost rather than at zero — the app does not invent a quote, and the em dash in the price column is what says so.
shares.unrealised.explain: Unrealised gain: what a position is worth today less what it cost you. It moves with the market and it is not money you have; carried at cost, a position with no observed price shows exactly zero rather than a loss.
shares.realised.explain: Realised gain: what your sales actually brought in, net of the fees on them and of the cost of the shares that left. It is a decomposition of your total gain and never a term to add to it — the proceeds are already in your cash.
shares.dividends.explain: Dividends received on this position, since the first event of your ledger. Fees taken on a payment are already deducted, and a position keeps this figure after it is sold.
shares.avgCost.explain: The unit cost of what you still hold, computed as the weighted average of your acquisitions with the fees on them absorbed — the French tax convention, and the app carries no other. A sale removes shares at that average and leaves it unchanged, so a closed position has no unit cost at all.

The three figures below are its terms and their sum is this number, so it can be checked by eye. It is a share of the figure at the top of the page, which counts every line you hold or have held.

accounts.rail.title: Weight of your accounts
accounts.rail.label: Your accounts
accounts.netContributed.explain: Net contributed: your deposits into this account less your withdrawals from it, fees excluded. It is the silent denominator of the two rates on this page, and it is what makes a gain of −0.62 € on 7,049.70 € legible as an account that went nowhere.
accounts.xirr.explain: Money-weighted return: what your deposits into this account actually earned. It is the single annual rate that reconciles everything that entered and left, each on its own date, with what the account is worth today — so it counts when you paid in, and it is annualised since the beginning rather than over the range above. Returns are computed from the dates of your events.
accounts.performance.explain: How the holdings themselves did over the range shown, deposits and withdrawals moving it by nothing at all. Every account starts at 100 on the first day of that range, which is what makes them comparable — a stored index counted from 2019 beside one counted from 2024 shares a unit without being a comparison. Read it against its range and never on its own: the same two accounts change places four times over seven ranges, every figure correct. Returns are computed from the dates of your events.
accounts.reason.withoutCashLedger: no cash movement recorded on this account
accounts.default.label: Unassigned
accounts.default.reassign: Assign these events to an account
accounts.detail.gainTotal.explain: What this account is worth less what you have paid into it — and the four figures under it are what it is made of, not a detail: their sum is the total. An account can go nowhere because an unrealised loss and a realised gain cancel out, and that is what this block shows. It covers the closed positions of this account too, and never the fees taken from your transfers on another one.
accounts.detail.curve.title: Value against what you have paid in
accounts.detail.dividends.explain: What this account has actually paid you, cash in hand — the closed positions of this account included, since a line that was sold kept the dividends it paid while it was held. It is one of the four terms of the total P&L above, promoted here because it is the one figure that answers on its own what this account has paid its owner.
accounts.detail.lines.link: {count, plural, one {See this account’s line on Shares} other {See this account’s # lines on Shares}}
accounts.detail.fromFile: Declared by an imported file, so it is read-only here: correct the file and drop it again, or forget its import.
accounts.remove.title: Remove this account
accounts.remove.offered: Nothing names this account and no file declares it, so removing it takes nothing with it. It cannot be undone from the app.
accounts.remove.seeded: This is the account every install has: every event naming no other is recorded there. Rename it rather than remove it.
accounts.remove.namedByEvents: {count, plural, one {# event names this account} other {# events name this account}}, and an account an event names cannot go: the event would then name something that does not exist. Assign them to another account, or remove them first.
accounts.remove.fromFile: An imported file declares it: forget that import to remove it.
accounts.reassign.title: Events assigned to no account
accounts.reassign.body: {count, plural, one {# event was recorded before you declared anything, so it names no account of yours.} other {# events were recorded before you declared anything, so they name no account of yours.}} Assign them to one of your accounts. Your files stay as they are — the column was right when they were imported, and it is this app that changed the rule underneath them.
accounts.form.reassign: {count, plural, one {Assign the # event that names no account to it} other {Assign the # events that name no account to it}}
accounts.form.reassign.hint: They were recorded before anything was declared, so they carry the account every install is given. This is the moment to move them: an imported event names its account for good afterwards.
accounts.form.create.title: A new account
accounts.form.edit.title: This account
accounts.form.description: An account is where your events are recorded, and it is yours to name. It has no currency of its own: every figure in this app is reported in one currency.
accounts.form.id.fixed: This is what your events name, in a file as well as here, so it cannot be changed. Declare another account and forget the import that carried this one instead.
accounts.form.label: Name
accounts.empty.title: No account declared
accounts.empty.body: Every install owns one account, so this screen means the declaration has not been read rather than that you have none. Declare one here, or hand the app a file that names your accounts.

data.notices.empty.title: Nothing to report
data.notices.empty.body: This installation has nothing to tell you. When it does — a file this version no longer reads, amounts it had to assume a currency for — it is written here, with the day it was noticed.

data.ledger.end: The end of the ledger · {count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}}
data.search.label: Search
data.search.placeholder: A ticker, a label, an account
data.filter.symbols: Reduced to {count, plural, one {one security} other {# securities}}: {symbols}
data.reduced: {named, select, yes {Reduced to {type} events matching “{subject}” on account {account}.} other {Reduced to {type} events on account {account}.}}
data.filter.none.title: No event matches
data.filter.none.body: Nothing you have recorded answers this search. Widen it, or clear the filters.
data.form.create.title: A new event
data.form.edit.title: This event
data.form.description: A portfolio is a ledger of dated events: say what happened, then when and how much.
data.form.date.explain: Returns are computed from the dates of your events. Both of them read the dates recorded here, and neither can tell a date you were sure of from one you estimated — so if you no longer have it, record your best estimate and read those two figures knowing that.
data.form.date.unreadable: Nothing is recorded without a readable date: write it as YYYY-MM-DD. A date field erases what it could not read, and says nothing about it.
data.form.account.unassigned: You have declared no account, so this event is recorded there — as every event that names none is. Declare one below the ledger to sort them.
data.form.account.pending: The list of your accounts has not arrived yet.
data.form.account.failed: Your accounts could not be read, so there is nothing to choose from here.
data.form.grantPrice.explain: Left empty, the award is a dilution: it adds shares and nothing else — nothing paid in, nothing it cost you. Filled, the value you declare feeds both at once: the shares enter your contributions and your cost basis together, so the position starts with no unrealised gain rather than with a gain equal to its whole value.
data.form.required: This kind of event needs this field.
data.empty.file.title: Import a file
data.empty.file.body: Hand the app a .csv or an .xlsx of your events. It reads it once, whatever it is called, and a file covering one year only is a legitimate start.
data.empty.manual.title: Enter a first event
data.empty.manual.body: A position is typed as the events that built it — a purchase, its date, its price. If you no longer have the date, record your best estimate.
data.imports.title: Import and export
data.drop.title: Import a .csv or an .xlsx
data.drop.body: Drop it here, or choose it. The app reads it once, whatever it is called, and its rows become events like any other — editable and removable one at a time.
data.import.duplicates: Write the lines already in my ledger
data.imports.forget.blocked: {count, plural, one {# event names an account this file declares} other {# events name accounts this file declares}}: forget those imports first.
data.imports.highlighted: Where the line you came from was imported from.
data.imports.show: Show this file under Import and export
data.imports.confirm.title: Forget {file}?
data.imports.confirm.effect: Removes {events, plural, one {# event} other {# events}}, {symbols, plural, one {# security} other {# securities}} and {accounts, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}} from your allocation.
data.imports.confirm.effect.accounts: Removes {accounts, plural, one {# declared account} other {# declared accounts}} from your allocation. No event came from this file.
data.imports.confirm.reimport: Re-importable if you still have the file. The app cannot tell: the import folder is optional, and the store is the only truth it holds.
data.imports.confirm.frees: {count, plural, one {No event will name {accounts} any more: that account becomes removable — or the import declaring it, forgettable — without this gesture touching it.} other {No event will name {accounts} any more: those accounts become removable — or the imports declaring them, forgettable — without this gesture touching them.}}
data.export.title: Export
data.export.two: A round trip needs two files: a file is an accounts source or an event source according to its header, never both. The events file carries the currency your amounts are recorded in, in a column of its own, so a file written before that column existed still imports unchanged.
data.export.workbook: A workbook, one sheet per year
data.export.selection: The filtered selection ({count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}})
data.bulk.title: Delete these {count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}}
data.bulk.confirm.title: Delete {count, plural, one {# event} other {# events}}?
data.bulk.confirm.body: Everything the reduction below retains leaves the ledger, whatever brought it in — the rows a file carried included.
data.bulk.confirm.undo: There is no undo, and no wastebasket: your backup is the export.
installation.advisory.unread_environment: {count, plural, one {# environment variable is set and read by nothing} other {# environment variables are set and read by nothing}}: {variables}. The settings they named live in the store since v5 — set them on the settings page, or with one PUT /api/settings — and those that were removed have no replacement at all. Unset them, or acknowledge this notice.
Environment variables are set that this version reads for nothing.
installation.advisory.reconstruction_run: The historical reconstruction is running: {complete, plural, one {# series has reached its first acquisition} other {# series have reached their first acquisition}} out of {total, number}. Your performance figures are computed from the history stored so far and will keep moving until it is complete.
The historical reconstruction has not reached every first acquisition.
installation.advisory.assumed_base_curre: Your amounts were read as {base}. {events, plural, one {# event} other {# events}} on {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} quoted in {currencies} ({symbols}) were imported before any price had been observed, so this version took the amounts in your files to be {base} already. If your broker exported them in the security's own currency, re-export those lines in {base} and drop the file again; if they were already in {base}, acknowledge this notice.
Amounts imported from files were taken to be in the base currency.
installation.settings.imposed.note: These are read when the app starts and cannot be answered from here. Changing one means recreating the container.
installation.settings.imposed.default: not set, the app's own value
installation.settings.saved: {count, plural, one {# setting saved} other {# settings saved}}. {now, plural, =0 {No share was re-armed} one {# share was re-armed} other {# shares were re-armed}}; {later, plural, =0 {none others are waiting for a market to open} one {# other will read the new value when its market opens} other {# others will read the new value when their markets open}}.
installation.settings.unchanged: Nothing had moved, so nothing was written.
installation.settings.refused: The app refused these values and wrote none of them.
settings.regular_interval.hint: How often a share whose market is open is asked for its price.
settings.backfill_interval.hint: How often the historical rebuild takes its next step.
settings.backfill_delay.hint: A courtesy to the price source, at the moment the app asks it the most.
settings.backfill_chunk_days.hint: How much history one rebuild request covers.
settings.staleness_horizon.hint: How long a stored price may stay frozen while the market moves before it is reported. 0 turns the check off.
settings.base_currency.hint: The one currency every figure is reported in.
settings.cadence.reach: Saving this applies to {now, plural, one {# share} other {# shares}} now, and to {later, plural, =0 {none others} one {# other when its market opens} other {# others when their markets open}}.
settings.backoff.retroactive: A share the app has failed to price waits a multiple of this number before it is tried again, so changing it rescales that wait retroactively — including for a share that has been failing since this morning.
installation.store.persistence: {state, select, persistent {This path is on a mount that outlives the container.} ephemeral {This path is inside the container and is lost when it is recreated.} other {Whether this path outlives the container cannot be observed here.}}
installation.store.ephemeral.title: This container keeps nothing
installation.store.ephemeral.body: The store sits in the container's own writable layer, so everything you record disappears the next time it is recreated. That is a fine way to try the app out. To keep it, mount a volume on this path and start it again.
installation.store.size.note: Purging returns rows, not bytes: the store reuses its own blocks, so this figure does not go down when something is removed from it.
installation.store.orphans: {count, plural, one {# share nothing declares any more} other {# shares nothing declares any more}}
installation.store.orphans.body: Their price history was kept when their events left, because forgetting an import can be undone by dropping the file again and a rebuilt history cannot. A position you have sold is not one of these — its events are still recorded.
problem.storageUnavailable: The data cannot be read right now. The app is running, its store is not answering.
problem.notFound: The app answered that this does not exist.
problem.badRequest: The app refused the request this page made.
problem.conflict: The app refused: what this names is already there, or something still rests on it.
problem.unreplayableLedger: The app refused and changed nothing: the ledger this gesture would leave sells shares it does not hold.
problem.unreplayableLedger.write: The app refused and wrote nothing: this sells {wanted, plural, one {{wanted, number, ::.####} share} other {{wanted, number, ::.####} shares}} of {symbol}, and your ledger holds {owned, number, ::.####} of them that day.
problem.unreplayableLedger.remove: The app refused and removed nothing: a later sale of {symbol} rests on this — it sells {wanted, plural, one {{wanted, number, ::.####} share} other {{wanted, number, ::.####} shares}}, and {owned, number, ::.####} would be left.
problem.invalidFile: The app refused this file and wrote nothing. Check that it is an event ledger, that the accounts it names are declared, and that its columns are the ones the export writes.
problem.tooLarge: This file is larger than the app takes in one go. Export a narrower range, or split it.
problem.internal: The app hit an error it did not expect.
problem.unreachable: The app is not answering. Nothing on screen comes from it.
